blocks.h: Where rinse water reaches the device
blocks.intro: Implants, surgical instruments, catheters and tubing, and ophthalmic devices meet this water after cleaning. The same loop can feed in vitro diagnostic reagent and ophthalmic solution preparation, passivation rinses and steam sterilizer feed: [confirm].

points.d: Washers filling at once drop loop pressure. We size storage and pumps to your fill profile.
Specification and sample point here; any point-of-use filter integrity tested, changed on data.
Warm water standing between batches grows biofilm; validate a drain-and-refill rule.

items.q: Do we need WFI for our final rinse?
items.a: Not usually; your risk assessment decides. WFI is common for cerebrospinal fluid contact. For blood or lymph contact, PW with a written endotoxin limit is usual.

items.q: Our rinse water meets USP PW. Is that enough for implants?
items.a: No, not on its own. The Purified Water (PW) monograph sets no endotoxin limit, and its microbial action level (USP <1231>) is guidance only. Write both into your water specification and sample at the washer inlet.

items.q: Is the water system validated or qualified?
items.a: Qualified. You validate the cleaning process (ISO 13485:2016, 7.5.6). The water system is qualified by installation and operational qualification (IQ, OQ), then performance qualification (PQ) from routine sampling.

items.q: Is hospital reprocessing water the same grade as ours?
items.a: No. Hospital reprocessing water is critical water under ANSI/AAMI ST108:2023, a different grade from Purified Water. Our hospital scope is confirmed when you enquire.
